source_metadata.title: Emergency Department Management of Acute Venous Thromboembolism in Patients With Obesity With Intravenous Unfractionated Heparin and Anti-Xa Monitoring
source_metadata.source_type: research article; single-center retrospective observational cohort

atoms.canonical_statement: The study compared time to the first therapeutic UFH anti-Xa level in adults with obesity and acute suspected VTE treated in the ED using total body weight versus adjusted body weight dosing, and also examined clinical outcomes.
This was a single-center retrospective observational study conducted in the Northwestern Memorial Hospital emergency department using patients treated from April 1, 2018 through January 31, 2020.
Eligible patients were 18–89 years old, had BMI greater than 30 kg/m², had suspected VTE diagnosed in the ED, and were managed with IV UFH using institutional anti-Xa monitoring.

population.label: Patients screened for the retrospective cohort
inclusion_criteria: IV UFH managed with anti-Xa levels per institutional protocol

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients were excluded for non-VTE UFH indications, DOAC or LMWH use within 72 hours, warfarin use within 72 hours with INR ≥1.4, or protocol noncompliance including anti-Xa timing or UFH rate-adjustment deviations.

population.label: Patients screened for the retrospective cohort
exclusion_criteria: DOAC or LMWH in prior 72 hours
Warfarin in prior 72 hours with INR ≥1.4
Deviation from institutional UFH rate-adjustment policy

atoms.canonical_statement: The institutional initial UFH regimen was an 80 units/kg bolus followed by an 18 units/kg/hr infusion, with no maximum bolus dose or infusion rate specified.
For anti-Xa 0.3–0.7 units/mL, the UFH rate was unchanged and anti-Xa was rechecked in 6 hours; after two consecutive therapeutic results, monitoring changed to daily.
For anti-Xa below 0.2 units/mL, the protocol gave a 25 units/kg bolus, increased the infusion by 3 units/kg/hr, and repeated anti-Xa in 6 hours.
For anti-Xa 0.2–0.29 units/mL, the protocol gave no bolus, increased the infusion by 2 units/kg/hr, and repeated anti-Xa in 6 hours.
For anti-Xa 0.71–0.8 units/mL, the protocol decreased the infusion by 1 unit/kg/hr and repeated anti-Xa in 6 hours.
For anti-Xa 0.81–0.99 units/mL, the protocol decreased the infusion by 2 units/kg/hr and repeated anti-Xa in 6 hours.
For anti-Xa at least 1 unit/mL, the protocol held UFH for 1 hour, then decreased the infusion by 3 units/kg/hr and repeated anti-Xa in 6 hours.
The first recorded ED weight was used for initial UFH dosing and adjustment; adjusted body weight was calculated as IBW + 0.4 × (TBW − IBW).
The institution had no policy directing use of TBW versus AdjBW; the ED pharmacist selected the dosing weight during order verification.
The primary outcome was time from UFH infusion initiation to the first therapeutic anti-Xa level, with therapeutic anti-Xa defined as 0.3–0.7 units/mL.

concept.text: Time to first therapeutic UFH anti-Xa level

outcome.measurement_method: Anti-Xa assay; time measured from UFH infusion initiation

atoms.canonical_statement: Secondary efficacy outcomes included BMI classification, UFH bolus dose, maintenance infusion rates, and the proportion reaching a therapeutic anti-Xa level within 24 hours.

concept.text: Secondary UFH efficacy and dosing outcomes

outcome.definition: BMI class, UFH bolus dose, maintenance infusion rate, and therapeutic anti-Xa within 24 hours

atoms.canonical_statement: Major bleeding was defined as fatal bleeding, symptomatic bleeding in a critical area or organ, a hemoglobin decrease of at least 2 g/dL, or transfusion of at least 2 units of whole blood or red blood cells.

concept.text: Major bleeding

outcome.definition: Fatal bleeding; symptomatic bleeding in a critical area/organ; hemoglobin fall ≥2 g/dL; or transfusion of ≥2 units whole blood/red blood cells

atoms.canonical_statement: Safety outcomes included first anti-Xa above 0.7 units/mL, major and non-major bleeding, protamine administration, thrombotic events, and mortality; thrombotic events included VTE propagation, myocardial infarction, or stroke.

concept.text: Composite set of prespecified safety outcomes

outcome.definition: Supratherapeutic first anti-Xa, bleeding, protamine, thrombosis, and mortality; thrombosis included VTE propagation, MI, or stroke

atoms.canonical_statement: Continuous variables were analyzed with Mann–Whitney U or Kruskal–Wallis tests, categorical variables with Fisher exact or chi-squared tests, and statistical significance was set at P<0.05.
Of 219 charts reviewed, 32 patients met inclusion criteria and were analyzed; the cohort had a median age of 50 years and 20 of 32 patients (62.5%) were male.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors interpreted the lower per-total-body-weight therapeutic infusion rate in the higher-BMI AdjBW group as consistent with the concept that UFH requirements may not increase proportionally with excess body weight.

The authors concluded that efficacy and safety outcomes were similar between TBW and AdjBW dosing and suggested that either dosing strategy may be used for adults with obesity presenting to the ED with acute VTE.
The authors identified the retrospective design, small sample size, and single-center setting as limitations that reduce the study’s accuracy and generalizability.
Only one BMI class III patient was dosed using TBW, limiting conclusions about TBW versus AdjBW dosing specifically in class III obesity.
Weights used for UFH dosing may have been estimated or patient-reported rather than obtained by objective weighing.
The primary endpoint used the first therapeutic anti-Xa level rather than consecutive therapeutic levels, which the authors stated limits the accuracy of the findings.
Because of the retrospective design, the investigators could not determine whether some supratherapeutic anti-Xa values resulted from inappropriate sampling from the line used for heparin infusion.
The authors declared no potential conflicts of interest related to the research, authorship, or publication.
The authors reported receiving no financial support for the research, authorship, or publication.

extraction_limitations: The study is observational and dosing-weight selection was made by ED pharmacists rather than randomized; atoms preserve this as a reported method rather than inferring causal equivalence.
The TBW and AdjBW groups differed substantially in body weight, BMI, and BMI-class distribution; baseline imbalance is extracted explicitly rather than treated as an adjusted comparison.

Table 3 and the Results narrative disagree on the P value for the BMI-class comparison of time to therapeutic anti-Xa (0.972 vs 0.927); the discrepancy is retained as a separate extractor-inference atom and not silently reconciled.
No data-availability statement was identified in the article text.
Atoms are machine-extracted and marked needs_review; validation establishes structural/sufficiency compliance, not human verification of clinical interpretation.
